timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: Microservices sound like a mess of moving parts.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: They are. And each moving part is a security seam you must secure.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: How do services trust each other?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Service identity with mutual TLS. Every service proves who it is to every other.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: An API gateway. Auth, rate limiting, input validation, all in one place.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: No. Decentralized authorization — every service enforces its own access rules.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: A layer that enforces policy and encrypts traffic between services automatically.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: How do I stop a failure from spreading?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Circuit breakers. A failing dependency stops being called before it takes everything down.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Distributed tracing correlates one request across every service it touches.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: Should I trust the internal network?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Never. One compromised service will try to hop to the next. Secure every seam.
